# package mqtt

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-openadr/notification/mqtt"
```

Package mqtt is the MQTT binding of OpenADR 3 notifications, for both sides: Publisher sends a VTN's notifications to a broker, and Subscriber receives them in a client.

The broker is not part of this module: a VTN that notifies by MQTT runs one, and its access control decides who may read which topic. See SECURITY.md.

## Types

### type Broker

```go
type Broker struct {
	// URL is the address of the broker: mqtt://host:1883 or mqtts://host:8883.
	URL string
	// ClientID identifies this client to the broker. Two connections with
	// the same ID take each other's place, so it has to be unique among the
	// clients of the broker. When empty the broker assigns one.
	ClientID string
	Username string
	Password string
	// TLS configures a connection to an mqtts URL; the defaults of
	// crypto/tls when nil.
	TLS *tls.Config
	// Backoff is the wait before a second attempt to connect, doubled for
	// each one after, up to a minute; 1 second when zero. It is also the
	// wait, doubled in the same way, before connecting again after a
	// connection that was lost: a broker that drops every connection at
	// once is not dialled again at once.
	Backoff time.Duration
}
```

Broker says how to reach and log in to a broker.

### type Metrics

```go
type Metrics interface {
	// OnConnected is called when a connection to the broker is made, and,
	// for a Subscriber, the subscriptions with it.
	OnConnected()
	// OnDisconnected is called when a connection is lost or given up, with
	// the reason.
	OnDisconnected(err error)
	// OnPublished is called when the broker has confirmed a notification.
	OnPublished()
	// OnDropped is called when a notification is not queued, because the
	// queue is full: the broker has been away for too long.
	OnDropped()
	// OnReceived is called for every notification a Subscriber hands to
	// its Notify function.
	OnReceived()
}
```

Metrics receives a callback for what a Publisher or a Subscriber does. A Publisher calls OnPublished and OnDropped, a Subscriber OnReceived, and both the two about the connection. The callbacks run on the goroutines of the Publisher or Subscriber and must not block. Implementations must be safe for concurrent use.

### type Publisher

```go
type Publisher struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

Publisher sends notifications to a broker, in the order they were given, at QoS 1. While the broker cannot be reached they wait, up to the size of the queue, and the connection is tried again.

Delivery to the broker is at least once while the Publisher runs. It is not durable: what is queued when the process stops is lost. What the broker does for a client that is not connected is the broker's business; with the clean sessions the Subscriber of this package uses, such a client misses the message.

A Publisher is safe for concurrent use. Close it to stop it.

#### func NewPublisher

```go
func NewPublisher(cfg PublisherConfig) (*Publisher, error)
```

NewPublisher returns a running Publisher. It does not wait for the broker: the connection is made in the background.

#### func (Publisher) Close

```go
func (p *Publisher) Close(ctx context.Context) error
```

Close stops accepting notifications and waits until those that are queued have reached the broker, or until ctx ends, whichever is first.

#### func (Publisher) Publish

```go
func (p *Publisher) Publish(topic string, body []byte)
```

Publish queues a notification for a topic and returns at once.

### type PublisherConfig

```go
type PublisherConfig struct {
	Broker
	// Queue is the number of notifications that may wait; 1024 when zero. A
	// notification for a full queue is dropped.
	Queue int
	// Logger receives connection failures and dropped notifications. Nil
	// disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Metrics receives a callback for what happens; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
}
```

PublisherConfig configures a Publisher.

### type Subscriber

```go
type Subscriber struct {

	// closed while subscribed

	// calling is held while Notify runs, so that Close can wait for it.

}
```

Subscriber receives the notifications a VTN publishes on a broker. It keeps the connection up: when it is lost, it connects and subscribes again.

What is published while the Subscriber is not connected is missed: it uses clean sessions. A message may arrive twice. As with webhooks, a client that must not miss a change still polls from time to time, and does so after every reconnect; Connected tells when.

#### func NewSubscriber

```go
func NewSubscriber(cfg SubscriberConfig) (*Subscriber, error)
```

NewSubscriber returns a running Subscriber. It does not wait for the broker; use Ready for that.

#### func (Subscriber) Close

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Close() error
```

Close disconnects and stops the Subscriber. Notify is not called after Close has returned.

#### func (Subscriber) Ready

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Ready(ctx context.Context) error
```

Ready waits until the Subscriber is connected and subscribed: from then on, what the VTN publishes is received.

#### func (Subscriber) Sessions

```go
func (s *Subscriber) Sessions() int
```

Sessions is the number of times the Subscriber has connected and subscribed. It grows by one with every reconnect: a client that polls after a reconnect watches it.

### type SubscriberConfig

```go
type SubscriberConfig struct {
	Broker
	// Topics are the topic filters to subscribe to, as a VTN names them in
	// its topic operations (see the MQTTTopics method of the clients).
	// Required.
	Topics []string
	// Notify is called for each notification, one at a time, in the order
	// the broker delivers them. Required. It should return soon: nothing
	// else is received meanwhile.
	Notify func(ctx context.Context, topic string, n openadr.Notification)
	// Logger receives connection failures and messages that are not
	// notifications. Nil disables logging.
	Logger *slog.Logger
	// Metrics receives a callback for what happens; see Metrics. Nil
	// disables them.
	Metrics Metrics
}
```

SubscriberConfig configures a Subscriber.
